panels.title: Sessions by Login (top 15)
panels.description: User sessions per login (sqlserver_sessions_by_login); system sessions are excluded

panels.title: Long-running User Requests
panels.description: User requests running for at least N seconds (sqlserver_requests_long_running)

panels.title: Longest Running Request by Command
panels.description: Elapsed time of the longest running user request per command (sqlserver_request_max_elapsed_seconds). WAITFOR/BACKUP can be long by design.

panels.title: Open Transactions
panels.description: Oldest open user transaction (left, seconds) and sessions sleeping with an open transaction (right)

panels.title: Top Queries (by CPU)
panels.description: Requires the opt-in top_queries collector (--collector.top_queries); the statement column needs --collector.top_queries.include_text. Rates over 5m, sorted by CPU.

defaults.noValue: top_queries collector disabled or no data

panels.title: Index Fragmentation (most fragmented)
panels.description: Requires the opt-in index_fragmentation collector (--collector.index_fragmentation). Collected in the background every few hours, not on each scrape; only indexes above min_page_count. Empty index name = heap.

defaults.noValue: index_fragmentation collector disabled or not collected yet

panels.description: Role and synchronization health per availability replica. Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.
panels.title: Replica State

panels.description: Per database replica: synchronization state, suspension, lag and queues. Queues are absent while data movement is suspended (SQL Server reports NULL). Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.
panels.title: Database Replica State
Data Movement & Sync State
panels.description: Red = suspended / not synchronizing. A suspended secondary makes the log send queue disappear and the primary's log grow (see Log Used). Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.

targets.expr: max by (sqlserver_instance, db_name) (sqlserver_database_log_used_percent) and on (db_name) max by (db_name) (sqlserver_hadr_database_synchronization_state{ag_name=~"$ag"})

panels.title: Log Used (AG databases)
panels.description: Transaction log usage of databases in the selected AGs, per instance. The log cannot be truncated while a secondary is behind or suspended.

panels.title: Log Send Queue
panels.description: Log not yet sent to the secondary. Absent while data movement is suspended. Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Redo Queue
panels.description: Log received but not yet redone on the secondary. Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Secondary Lag
panels.description: Seconds the secondary is behind the primary, as reported on the primary (SQL Server 2016+). Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Mirroring Session
panels.description: Role, state, transaction safety and witness per mirrored database, as reported by the principal. On the mirror, sys.database_mirroring is NULL unless the login is sysadmin, so the mirror usually has no row here. Aggregated across every exporter (a mirror without sysadmin reports no session state), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Mirroring Role & State
panels.description: Role swaps show failovers; red = suspended / disconnected / not synchronized. Aggregated across every exporter (a mirror without sysadmin reports no session state), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Mirroring Log Send Queue
panels.description: Log not yet sent to the mirror (grows while suspended, disconnected or during large transactions). Both partners report it, each from its own view. Aggregated across every exporter (a mirror without sysadmin reports no session state), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Mirroring Redo Queue
panels.description: Log received but not yet redone on the mirror. Both partners report it, each from its own view. Aggregated across every exporter (a mirror without sysadmin reports no session state), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Mirroring Avg Commit Delay
panels.description: Average time each transaction waited for the mirror to acknowledge the commit (high-safety mode; ~0 when SAFETY OFF). Empty without write transactions. Aggregated across every exporter (a mirror without sysadmin reports no session state), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Mirroring Log Throughput
panels.description: Log sent by the principal, received and redone by the mirror. Aggregated across every exporter (a mirror without sysadmin reports no session state), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Mirrored Write Transactions/sec
panels.description: Transactions that wrote to the mirrored database and waited for the log to be sent to the mirror. Aggregated across every exporter (a mirror without sysadmin reports no session state), so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Log Shipping Primary
panels.description: Time since the last log backup taken by the log shipping backup job vs. the alert threshold configured in SQL Server. Requires the opt-in log_shipping collector (--collector.log_shipping). Values come from the log shipping monitor tables of the primary, secondary and monitor server; the freshest timestamp wins, so the instance selector does not apply here.

targets.expr: (time() - max by (primary_server, primary_database) (sqlserver_log_shipping_primary_last_backup_timestamp_seconds)) > bool max by (primary_server, primary_database) (sqlserver_log_shipping_primary_backup_threshold_seconds)

panels.title: Log Shipping Secondary
panels.description: Time since the last copy and restore on the secondary, latency of the last restored backup and the restore alert threshold configured in SQL Server. Requires the opt-in log_shipping collector (--collector.log_shipping). Values come from the log shipping monitor tables of the primary, secondary and monitor server; the freshest timestamp wins, so the instance selector does not apply here.

targets.expr: time() - max by (secondary_server, secondary_database, primary_server, primary_database) (sqlserver_log_shipping_secondary_last_copied_timestamp_seconds)
time() - max by (secondary_server, secondary_database, primary_server, primary_database) (sqlserver_log_shipping_secondary_last_restored_timestamp_seconds)

(time() - max by (secondary_server, secondary_database, primary_server, primary_database) (sqlserver_log_shipping_secondary_last_restored_timestamp_seconds)) > bool max by (secondary_server, secondary_database, primary_server, primary_database) (sqlserver_log_shipping_secondary_restore_threshold_seconds)

panels.title: Time Since Last Log Backup (primary)
panels.description: Grows until the next log shipping backup; crossing the threshold line means backups stopped. Requires the opt-in log_shipping collector (--collector.log_shipping). Values come from the log shipping monitor tables of the primary, secondary and monitor server; the freshest timestamp wins, so the instance selector does not apply here.

targets.expr: time() - max by (secondary_server, secondary_database, primary_server, primary_database) (sqlserver_log_shipping_secondary_last_restored_timestamp_seconds)

panels.title: Time Since Last Restore (secondary)
panels.description: Grows until the next restore; crossing the threshold line means the secondary is falling behind (restore job stopped or failing). Requires the opt-in log_shipping collector (--collector.log_shipping). Values come from the log shipping monitor tables of the primary, secondary and monitor server; the freshest timestamp wins, so the instance selector does not apply here.

panels.title: Last Restore Latency
panels.description: Time between the creation of the last restored log backup on the primary and its restore on the secondary (minute precision). Requires the opt-in log_shipping collector (--collector.log_shipping). Values come from the log shipping monitor tables of the primary, secondary and monitor server; the freshest timestamp wins, so the instance selector does not apply here.
